clue.text: Period when stuffed shirt finally gets seduced by bribe?

parts.note: stuffed with food means full

indicators.note: being seduced is being taken in, so the bribe takes in the letter

parts.note: a sop is a small bribe or concession to keep someone quiet

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word shirt

explanation.surface: A pompous person finally succumbs to a bribe: when does the corruption happen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets seduced by' puts T (last letter of 'shirt') inside SOP. 'Stuffed shirt' reads as one phrase, a pompous person, but the words split into separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a period, the punctuation mark ending a sentence, is called by this name.

clue.text: Answer given by department's experts

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, with the possessive giving the S

explanation.surface: A department's specialists supply the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adepts are people highly skilled in a field, so the word is a synonym for experts.

clue.text: Angry Face? Here, you can stuff that!

indicators.note: something angry is worked up and agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An Angry Face emoji tells someone where to stuff it, in the puzzle's emoji theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry Face' is the name of an emoji, but 'Angry' is the anagram signal. 'stuff' plays on its rude sense; here it means stuff your face with food.
explanation.definitionFit: A small restaurant serving snacks and drinks is a place where diners can fill themselves with food.

clue.text: One that's imitating diva, framing 'Love' with Red Heart on top

indicators.note: in a down answer, on top means placed before the rest
the heart of a word is its middle letter, here of Red
a frame goes round a picture, so the diva's name goes round the letter

parts.note: Cher is the famous pop diva
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A diva impersonator wraps 'Love' with a Red Heart emoji on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' puts O inside CHER to give CHOER; 'Heart' takes E from 'Red', placed 'on top'. 'Red Heart' is an emoji name, split here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who repeats or copies what others say or do echoes them, so this is an imitator.

clue.text: One 22D wasted going round university in African capital

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters go round, enclosing, the single letter
wasted means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: 22 down is the last word of the linked theme entry, a 24-hour period, so the phrase reads one day

explanation.surface: Someone spends a wasted day near a university in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: '22D' must be swapped for its answer before 'wasted' can shuffle the phrase; 'going round' then puts the university letter inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is the capital city of Cameroon in Central Africa.

clue.text: Like piano used for Killer Queen? Quite the opposite, allegedly

definitions.text: used for Killer Queen? Quite the opposite, allegedly

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Was a piano used on Queen's song Killer Queen? Rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like piano' reads AS P. Reverse the roles: not a piano used for Killer Queen but a killer used for a queen, Cleopatra, said to have died by snakebite; 'allegedly' since the story is uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: A small venomous snake of Egypt, legend says, was the killer that Cleopatra used on herself.

clue.text: At first such a large dog makes one 16!

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word such

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.surface: Such a big dog makes quite a leap!
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is the second half of the linked theme answer at 14, meaning a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A salchow is a figure-skating leap taking off from one back inside edge, named after Ulrich Salchow.

clue.text: Lout given Thumbs Up around lunchtime?

indicators.note: the approval letters sit around the time, enclosing it

parts.note: a thumbs-up sign means okay, written OK
lunch is often at one o'clock, and one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A lout is given the Thumbs Up emoji around lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunchtime as one o'clock, written as Roman I, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An oik is British slang for an uncouth, badly behaved person, a lout.

clue.text: Going back a bit, recall a poster showing one of the Stones

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in the reverse direction
a bit means only a part of the words recall a poster is taken

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a poster of one of the Rolling Stones from a while back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' takes LAPO from 'recall a poster'; 'Going back' turns it round. 'the Stones' hints at the Rolling Stones band, but means gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a precious gemstone known for its shifting play of colours.

clue.text: Two compositions for which payment is determined by amount produced

definitions.text: for which payment is determined by amount produced

parts.note: with compositions this asks for two words each meaning a composition; a piece is a musical composition
a work is a composition, as in a work by Mozart

explanation.surface: Two musical compositions commissioned with pay by output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two compositions' asks for two separate words meaning a composition: PIECE and WORK, joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecework is labour paid per item made rather than by the hour.

clue.text: Intelligence shown by ponies about to mature

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of ponies are rearranged

parts.note: to mature is to age

explanation.surface: Clever ponies are about to grow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes ESPION from 'ponies'. 'about to mature' reads as one phrase but splits: 'about' acts on 'ponies', 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of spying and gathering secret information on enemies.

clue.text: Ghost out of place in group dressed in black?

indicators.note: letters out of place are disordered, so ghost is rearranged

explanation.surface: A ghost looks out of place among people in black.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the goth subculture favour black clothes and dark make-up.

clue.text: Food not finished by setter dismissing starter as unappetising fare

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter of the food word is dropped

parts.note: grub is informal for food

indicators.note: dismissing the starter drops the opening letter of the setting word

parts.note: gel is something that sets, like a setting agent in cooking

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter leaves food half-eaten, skipping the starter of a bad meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler, but here means something that sets, GEL; 'starter' is its first letter, not a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin porridge of oats boiled in water or milk, the proverbial dreary workhouse meal.

clue.text: Wrongly made out it's Parma beef

indicators.note: something wrongly made out is misread, so the letters come out in another order

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly claimed a meat was Parma ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly made out' shuffles ITS PARMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a highly seasoned smoked cured beef, a deli staple.

clue.text: Shigetaka Kurita's invention originally, bound to provide springboard for long-running event?

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: Shigetaka Kurita, inventor of the emoji, was bound to launch an enduring phenomenon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long-running event' suggests something that lasts, but means an event of long-distance running down a ramp on skis.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep ramp from which skiers launch themselves to fly as far as possible, a takeoff for a long glide.

clue.text: Old Woman youthful chap in 50s married

parts.note: old woman is informal for mother, ma
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a young man of the 1950s British youth fashion

explanation.surface: A mother married a young man of the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style drape jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Mated means paired or coupled together, as partners joined in marriage.

clue.text: See 14
See 21
Length of old Lying Face, say

indicators.note: say means the letter is spoken, giving the sound of its name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying Face' is an emoji with a long nose; 'Face' takes L from 'Lying', and the letter L said aloud names an old unit.

clue.text: The very thing described by first appearances of Man Tipping Hand

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the two initials go round
first appearances means the opening letters of the words Man and Tipping

parts.note: it, as in 'that's it', means exactly the thing wanted

explanation.surface: The very thing the Man Tipping Hand emoji depicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man Tipping Hand' is an emoji name, split: initials M and T go round IT, and 'Hand' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mitt is slang for a hand, from mitten.

clue.text: Get soaked by rain out in China

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the friend word

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a friend

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters of rain are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Get drenched by rain while out in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns RAIN into ARIN, put 'in' MATE. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left steeping in a liquid seasoning absorbs it, as meat soaks in a mix before cooking.

clue.text: Rolling On The Floor Laughing initially — Hob's going to head up admiral's first fleet!

indicators.note: to head up is to lead, so the setter's piece comes in front of the next
rolling means tumbling about, so the initials are rearranged
initially means taking the first letter of each word that follows

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of admiral's

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling On The Floor Laughing' names the ROFL emoji, but 'Rolling' is the anagram signal on the next four initials. 'Hob' is this puzzle's setter, so his 'going to' is the contraction for I will.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats.

clue.text: Tutors working in school sometimes, but rarely

definitions.note: a plural noun: fish that sometimes swim in schools, with this plural form seldom used

indicators.note: working means operating or active, so the letters of tutors are reworked

explanation.surface: Tutors are sometimes at work in a school, but seldom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests teachers, but is a shoal of fish; 'rarely' notes this plural is uncommon, the usual plural being unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Freshwater game fish that can gather in a shoal; the -s plural is a rare variant form.

clue.text: Lost mojo weirdly, with ad for symbolic annual celebration

indicators.note: something lost is astray and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has weirdly lost their mojo turns to an advert for a yearly festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' shuffles MOJO WEIRDLY AD; 'weirdly' looks like the signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual date each July honouring the little pictograph symbols used in messages.

clue.text: Greeting 2 when cycling before tea

indicators.note: before means the cycled number comes ahead of the drink
cycling means the letters rotate, the last moving to the front

parts.note: the numeral 2 is the word two
cha is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: A cyclist calls out a greeting on the way to tea.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' looks like a reference to 2 down, but is just the number; 'cycling' moves its last letter to the front. Wotcha is informal British for hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Wotcha is a casual British hello, from 'what cheer'.

clue.text: Least upstanding spin doctor caught out importing baked food

indicators.note: importing means bringing something in, so the pastry dishes go inside
to spin is to twist about, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
pies are baked food

explanation.surface: A spin doctor, caught out, takes in baked goods while hardly standing up straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin doctor' reads as a PR man, but 'spin' is the anagram signal. 'caught out' removes C from the word doctor, and 'spin' turns DOTOR into DROOT before 'importing' acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Most drooping means sagging furthest, hence the least upright.

clue.text: See 21
Getting up, interrupted content Grinning Cat's sound observation?

clue.text: Almost knocked over hot drink

gin is an alcoholic drink

clue.text: Antelope found in growing numbers

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words growing numbers

explanation.surface: An antelope species is found in growing numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnu, or wildebeest, is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Aphrodisiac fare of novel sort? Yes

explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book or an adjective on 'sort' but shuffles SORT YES.

clue.text: Call for round gets you tense inside bar

indicators.note: inside means the two letters are placed within the drinks call
